chapter: Opening and who he played with
title: Piano job at the Oasis with Albert Francis and Hughes
summary: He played piano nine to three nightly for about two years at a nightclub with a Dixieland band including Albert Francis on drums and a sax player named Hughes; also Pico and Peter Williams.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it

blocks.x: Where was this place that you were playing on, Allen, Iowa? What's the name of that?
It was a nightclub. I forgot the name of that place too.
Where was the Oasis? The Oasis?

I played Frank Quintello. He was a Spanishman. Two Losing Decay. We played there. I played there about two years. I was playing piano. I played piano there. I was playing from nine to three every night.
What kind of band was it? I mean... Dixieland.

Yeah, and who else? I had Albert Francis playing drum. You know Albert. He used to play with Bruce Armstrong. And I had a fellow by the name of Hughes. He's playing the saxophone. What is his name? Hughes? Hughes. He was in the saxophone. Wallingford Hughes. Frenchie Hughes? I don't know what's his last name. I know his name was Hughes.
And... I have no copy of the family album. Who else? He's in the family album.

He's so many fellas out of the play, but... I can't think of all that damn. But... Alphonse Pico and Peter Williams. I played for Peter Williams too. Well, that was our violinist. Peter Williams was the lead man.
